decisions.reason: The counterexample labels injectivity as its Statement refuted, then proves E^5 is a nonzero kernel element. The definition consistently distinguishes generic inclusion from specialized noninjectivity, uses a valid localization map, and makes no higher-rank PBW claim.

The Statement explicitly assumes a specialized family with the cited divided-power multiplication, so F2 restates a hypothesis rather than extending the supplier theorem to arbitrary families. The block product (1+t^ell) and symmetric exponent congruences prove Lucas also for negative upper indices; multiplication then gives a! and the invertible residue factorial.

At c=1,t=2 the claimed Vandermonde identity has the wrong difference, so integral toral preservation was unproved. Replaced it by T(c,t)=q^(-t)T(c-1,t)+q^(c-t)K T(c-1,t-1), derived by factoring the toral product. Induction on t obtains T(0,t) from E^(t)F^(t), then all shifts in both directions using Laurent units. No statement or dependency changed.

The actual step 2.1 exponent is (a-r)(c-r)+r. At a=c=1 its r=0 coefficient is q and its r=1 coefficient is -q, giving zx=q xz-q y exactly as required by y=xz-q^(-1)zx. Its integral block spans, positivity induction, generic rank independence and base change remain valid after the proof-only toral repair in its braid supplier.

The injectivity sentence is explicitly the counterexample’s Statement refuted. Its proof agrees with this proposition. The rank-one supplier proves the localized ordinary presentation and free PBW basis before specialization; E^ell is therefore nonzero in the source, whereas the integral identity E^ell=[ell]!E^(ell) specializes to zero in the target. The generator assignment respects every rank-one relation.

The definition allowed reducible finite simply-laced systems while its category supplier selects a simple system and h was unspecified for unequal components. Preserved the full finite-type scope: h is the maximum component Coxeter number, full weight conditions apply to every component, and commuting integral component forms identify their tensor product by the integral triangular bases. Tensor coproduct, antipode and product pivot provide the stated duality for all finite modules, including modules not themselves pure tensors.

The cited flag supplier proves a separate highest-vector splitting lemma in proof step 1.1, beyond its standard-costandard vanishing statement. For an extension with quotient Delta(nu) and kernel Delta(mu), mu<nu, all weights are at most nu; lifting the highest line gives a highest vector and Weyl universality gives a section. This is precisely the adjacent reversed section used in 6.1. Checked the actual integral cyclic tensor presentation, saturated quotient, exact weight-functor projectives and reciprocity; componentwise category repair preserves them.

Proof 4.1 invokes the highest-vector splitting lemma, actually proved in its F2 supplier at step 1.1. Previously processed nu is not strictly below the new mu, so an extension of Delta(nu) by Delta(mu) has no weight strictly greater than nu. Its lifted top vector is highest and Weyl universality splits it, including incomparable labels and self extensions. Hence the universal extension kills the chosen Ext group and preserves all earlier vanishings. The finite heredity-trace/Tor argument proves the filtration criterion needed to finish the construction.

Its F4 explicitly cites the tilting-existence theorem, whose proof 4.1 constructs the finite universal extensions and whose 5.1 extracts the highest-label tilting summand. Reciprocity and Weyl strong linkage imply that a projective kernel at mu outside S has no Weyl section with label in S; hence Hom(kernel,X)=0 and Ext^1(Delta(mu),X)=0 whenever X has composition support in S. The cited finite construction therefore never adds a label outside S, justifying 8.1. Checked the baby-Verma residue recurrence, Frobenius socle, finite character coefficients and downward translations for both parameter orders.
